subject: Civil Engineering
title: Foundations: Where Bridges Begin
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Foundations: Where Bridges Begin.

hook.text: The Brooklyn Bridge's foundations were dug 78 feet underwater inside airtight boxes.

buildup.text: Caissons — watertight chambers — let workers dig in dry conditions below rivers.

discovery.text: Modern bridges use driven piles or drilled shafts to reach solid rock or firm soil.

twist.text: Scour — river currents washing soil from around piers — is a top cause of failure.

climax.text: Engineers armor foundations with riprap — heavy stones that resist erosion.

punchline.text: A bridge is only as strong as what it stands on.

quiz.question: What is scour in bridge engineering?
options: Rust forming on steel bridge components
River currents eroding soil from around bridge foundations
Wind vibrations that shake the bridge deck
